name: ziplark-mcp
description: Read, preview, grep, diff, hash, extract, add, rename, remove, convert & create archives — ZIP, RAR, 7z, tar, ISO, DEB, RPM, PKG, XAR, CAB — from an MCP client.
long_description: Ziplark's archive engine over the Model Context Protocol. Lists, reads/previews in memory, searches text across entries in memory (grep), compares two archives (diff), computes SHA-256/SHA-1/CRC32 digests (hash), extracts (including smart anti-tarbomb extraction), verifies, appends to, renames/moves entries inside, removes entries from, converts between formats, and creates archives (including multi-volume .001, .002, … split creation): ZIP (incl. .z01/.zip.001 split, .crx, .jar, .apk, .whl), RAR and RAR5 (including multi-volume sets, encrypted headers and self-extracting archives), 7z (incl. .7z.001 multi-volume), tar and the compressed-tar variants, single-stream gz/bz2/xz/zst/lz4, ISO 9660 / Joliet disc images, Debian (.deb) & Unix ar (.ar, .a), Red Hat (.rpm) & CPIO (.cpio.*), macOS Installer packages (.pkg, .mpkg) & XAR (.xar, .xip), and Microsoft Cabinet (.cab). Listings and in-memory file reads are paged so huge archives never flood the context, and every extraction path is funnelled through a single guard so no entry can escape the destination directory. Read tools (ziplark_info, ziplark_list, ziplark_read, ziplark_grep, ziplark_diff, ziplark_hash, ziplark_test) are always available; extracting, creating, appending, renaming, removing and converting require --allow-write.

tools.name: ziplark_info
tools.description: What kind of archive this is and what shape it is in: format, entry count, sizes, encryption, and — for a multi-volume set — its volumes, whether one is missing, whether it is solid, and its comment.

tools.name: ziplark_list
tools.description: List the entries inside an archive, paged, with per-directory counts when the result is truncated.

tools.name: ziplark_read
tools.description: Read a single entry inside an archive into memory without extracting anything to disk, with offset and max_bytes paging.

tools.name: ziplark_grep
tools.description: Full-text search across text files inside an archive in memory without writing anything to disk. Automatically skips binary entries and returns <path>:<line>:<text> matches.

tools.name: ziplark_diff
tools.description: Compare two archives of any readable format in memory without extracting to disk; reports added, removed, modified, and unchanged entries, with optional unified text diff patches.

tools.name: ziplark_hash
tools.description: Compute SHA-256, SHA-1, or CRC32 digests for entries inside an archive without writing anything to disk.

tools.name: ziplark_test
tools.description: Verify archive integrity by decompressing every entry. Writes nothing, and reports every bad entry rather than the first.

tools.name: ziplark_extract
tools.description: Extract an archive, or exactly the entries named, into a destination directory (with optional smart anti-tarbomb mode). Requires --allow-write.

tools.name: ziplark_create
tools.description: Create a ZIP (AES-256), 7z (AES-256) or tar archive from files and directories, with optional multi-volume split_size (.001, .002, …). Requires --allow-write.

tools.name: ziplark_add
tools.description: Add or replace files/directories inside an existing archive (zip, 7z, tar.*), or create it if it does not exist. Requires --allow-write.

tools.name: ziplark_remove
tools.description: Remove files or directories from an existing archive (zip, 7z, tar.*) in place. Requires --allow-write.

tools.name: ziplark_rename
tools.description: Atomically rename or move an entry or directory prefix inside an existing archive (zip, 7z, tar.*). Requires --allow-write.

tools.name: ziplark_convert
tools.description: Convert any readable archive (including RAR, CAB, DEB, RPM, PKG, XAR, 7z, ISO) directly into a .zip, .7z, or .tar.* archive while preserving permissions, symlinks, and modification times. Requires --allow-write.
